words.trans: v. 大怒，愤愤不平；发火，生闷气  n. 烟气，烟雾。心里憋着怒火，闷闷生气（小说高频，不一定爆发出来）
examples: She was still fuming about the injustice.
He fumed silently at the insult.

words.trans: adv. 心事重重地；若有所思地；带着忧思地
examples: She looked at the sky pensively.
He stared pensively out of the window.

words.trans: 固定搭配：调转方向奔赴某处（turn for + 地点）
examples: She was about to turn for home.
The ship turned for port.

words.trans: n. 刨花；薄片、细屑（shaving 复数，本义刨木头削下来的薄薄碎屑）
examples: The oars scooped up shavings of light.
Wood shavings curled from the plane.

words.trans: adj. 芬芳的，有特殊浓郁气味的（不一定是香，指辨识度很强的气味，这里是烟斗烟味）
examples: She caught the aromatic trail of smoke.
aromatic herbs.

words.trans: 一缕飘过来的烟（气味轨迹）
examples: She caught the aromatic trail of smoke.
A trail of smoke rose from the chimney.

words.trans: n. 丁香（香料，clove 复数）
examples: A mix of fresh straw, cloves, burnt toast.
Add two cloves to the sauce.

words.trans: 一瓣大蒜（a clove of garlic）
examples: Crush a clove of garlic.
Stir in a clove of garlic.

words.trans: adj. 成年人特有的；成熟的；属于大人的（grown-up scent 成年人的气息）
examples: The grown-up scent reached out to her.
She kept a grown-up calm.

words.trans: = but for（虚拟，要不是因为…）（If it weren’t for sb/sth）
examples: If it weren't for Tom, the Queen would be dead.
If it weren't for you, we'd be lost.

words.trans: 被大肆公开颂扬、被捧到人人皆知，到处夸（shout sth from the rooftops 站在屋顶大声喊→大肆宣扬、公开吹捧，所有人都听见）
examples: But who gets praised from the rooftops?
Their bravery should be praised from the rooftops.

words.trans: 不管口语书面都常见，不限于 thankful。To solve this, start by checking the battery. 要解决这个问题，可以先从检查电池入手；I’ll start by introducing myself. 我先做个自我介绍
examples: We could start by being thankful.
Let's start by introducing ourselves.

words.trans: 怀揣某个目标出发、立志要达成（强调出发时抱有的意图与目标）（set out to do sth）
examples: You achieved what you set out to do.
She set out to break the record.

words.trans: adj. 平静的；宁静的；安稳的
examples: The Teal sails these tranquil waters.
a tranquil lake at dawn.

words.trans: v. 推测；假定；认为；姑且认定
examples: I presume you didn't do it to be praised.
I presume you've heard the news.

words.trans: 是要付出代价的；并非毫无牺牲（come at a price）
examples: Saving people usually comes at a price.
Victory came at a price.

words.trans: adj. 傻乎乎的，鲁莽的，有点蠢（英式口语，语气不算很重，偏“行事冒失”，不是恶毒骂人）
examples: Tom may have made himself look a bit daft.
Don't be daft.

words.trans: v.【古】显露、暴露、浮出水面（这里是动词，不是副词！现代英语日常已不这么用）。The truth will out (in the end) 真相终会大白——经典老式英语谚语，英式文学小说常见
examples: The truth will out in the end.
The truth is bound to out.

words.trans: 亲自去看一看，自己亲眼核实，亲自求证。for myself 为我自己求得亲身见闻→亲自求证；by myself 靠我自己、单独一个人→独自干活、出行
examples: I intend to see for myself.
Let me see for myself.

words.trans: v. 为（人品）做担保、作证（vouch for）
examples: I'm going to vouch for Tom's character.
I can vouch for him.

words.trans: 非常地道高频口语（英美式都用）。first thing 本身副词性质短语，意思第一件事、一……就（优先立刻办）（I’ll ring you first thing tomorrow 我明天一早就给你打电话）。❌ the first thing tomorrow（啰嗦）❌ at first thing tomorrow（错误，不要加 at）
examples: I have an appointment first thing in the morning.
Call me first thing tomorrow.

words.trans: 卷入、牵涉进坏事；深陷其中（be mixed up in）
examples: If the authorities are mixed up in this.
He didn't want to be mixed up in a crime.

words.trans: 固定地道短语（口语常用）。察觉到某人的秘密/阴谋；盯上某人，发现对方的勾当（be on to sb）
examples: We're on to them.
The police are on to the gang.

words.trans: v. 使困惑；使茫然；让人摸不着头脑
examples: Maggie shook her head, bewildered.
The question bewildered everyone.

words.trans: 固定高频短语。有共同点；有相似之处（have sth in common）
examples: Tom and Ryan have more in common than you think.
We have nothing in common.

words.trans: brink n.（悬崖的）边缘；临界点。on the brink (of sth) 处在…的边缘；濒临（某种重大状态，通常是危险、崩溃的临界点）。on the brink of 濒临重大转折、文学感强，可毁灭也可重大改变；on the verge of 几乎就要，与之近义，日常更常用
examples: On the brink, trying to work out who he was.
on the brink of collapse.

words.trans: n. 冒险举动；出格的恶作剧；一场惊险的经历
examples: This little escapade was the jolt he needed.
a drunken escapade.

words.trans: n. 猛然的冲击；一记警醒
examples: This escapade was the jolt he needed.
a sudden jolt woke me up.

words.trans: v. 沉湎、耿耿于怀（反复琢磨自己的烦心事，郁郁不乐）。brood on sth 盯着这件事反复琢磨，放不下
examples: To stop brooding on his own problems.
Don't brood on past mistakes.

words.trans: adv. 极其；惊人地；轰动地；场面盛大可观地
examples: He saved others, spectacularly.
The plan failed spectacularly.

words.trans: n. 疯子；举止癫狂的人  adj. 疯狂的
examples: He would still have looked like a lunatic.
a lunatic scheme.

words.trans: 习语。字面像“算一算成本”，实际：预先考量、掂量一件事背后要承担的风险、损失与负面后果。重点：行动之前心里清楚这么干会付出多大代价，但依然选择去做
examples: He'd counted the cost.
They acted without counting the cost.

words.trans: adj. 薄如蝉翼的；轻盈纤细的  n. 薄纱；蛛丝
examples: A micro-light, gossamer wings backlit.
The spider's gossamer threads.

words.trans: adj. 逆光的；从背后照亮的
examples: Its gossamer wings backlit in the last rays.
a backlit photograph.

words.trans: = the last rays of the sun（省略 of the sun，小说常见简写），落日余晖、夕阳最后的光芒
examples: Gossamer wings backlit in the last rays.
The sun cast its last rays.

words.trans: n.【英式英语】刘海（额头前的那一小撮头发）。push the fringe out of her eyes 把垂下来的刘海拨开，不让它挡住眼睛
examples: Maggie pushed the fringe out of her eyes.
Her fringe fell over her eyes.

words.trans: digging 比喻义：调查、打探（不是拿铲子挖土）。a bit of digging 做一番深挖调查，去搜集线索，追查证据
examples: A bit of digging, before the trail goes cold.
A bit of digging turned up the truth.

words.trans: 线索冷却；追查断线；找不到痕迹了（the trail goes cold）
examples: Before the trail goes cold.
The trail had gone cold.

words.trans: n. 输水渠、高架引水管道（大型人工输水工程）
examples: The Thirlmere Aqueduct passes under the fell.
water is carried by an aqueduct.

words.trans: n. 水库，蓄水池
examples: An enormous man-made reservoir up the valley.
The town draws water from a reservoir.

words.trans: n. 狮子窝；龙潭虎穴，极度危险的地方（lion’s den）
examples: Don't go walking into the lion's den!
He walked back into the lion's den.

words.trans: n. 维多利亚时代的人（Victorians）
examples: The Victorians built it.
Amazing, those Victorians.

words.trans: = and + yet。and 承接上文、认可前面；yet 转折“可是仍然”。语感：先让步，再转折；比普通 but 更强调内心纠结矛盾，适合人物心理活动。可用 and yet 或只用 yet；不要写成 but yet（重复冗余）
examples: And yet, if no one ever went near the den.
He was tired, and yet he kept going.

words.trans: 侥幸逃脱，做坏事而不受惩罚（get away with sth。get away with everything 什么坏事都可以逍遥法外、全部脱罪）
examples: Those people would get away with everything.
He got away with a fine.

words.trans: n. 普通秋沙鸭（一种河上野鸭，母鸭头部有标志性橙红色羽冠）
examples: A female goosander with some newly hatched chicks.
A goosander dived for fish.

words.trans: v. 费力前行，吃力地干（英式拼写；labor 美式）。labour doing sth 费力做某事
examples: A female goosander was labouring upstream.
He laboured up the hill.

words.trans: n. 一丛；一簇羽毛/毛发
examples: Orange tufts glistening with jewels of water.
a tuft of grass.

words.trans: v.（湿润表面）闪闪发亮
examples: Orange tufts glistening with jewels of water.
Her eyes glistened with tears.

words.trans: 文学比喻，把水珠比作宝石（jewels of water）
examples: Orange tufts glistening with jewels of water.
The grass glittered with jewels of water.

words.trans: 向后退缩、往后缩（因为害怕）（shrink back）
examples: She shrank back from the barking dog.
The child shrank back into the corner.

words.trans: adj. 向外悬垂、挑出的（overhanging roof 向外挑出来的屋檐/顶棚）
examples: An overhanging roof.
overhanging branches.

words.trans: v. 随意搭、披挂在……上面
examples: She draped a scarf over her shoulders.
Cloth draped across the table.

words.trans: adj. 细长的；苗条纤细的；窄窄的
examples: Her slender fingers.
a slender path.

words.trans: 短语：镶嵌、布满，上面密密麻麻装着很多东西（be studded with sth）
examples: The shore was studded with rocks.
a sky studded with stars.

words.trans: n.[复数 straps] 绑带、系带、捆扎带（尼龙/织带这种扁平结实带子）
examples: She tightened the straps on her pack.
a camera strap.

words.trans: adj. 有节奏的
examples: The rhythmic sound of the oars.
a rhythmic drumming.

words.trans: n. 鸡皮疙瘩（复数）
examples: The cold gave her goosebumps.
It sent goosebumps down her arms.

words.trans: n. 漩涡，回水涡流
examples: A leaf spun in the eddy.
The boat drifted into an eddy.

words.trans: 短语：（伤口）愈合、长好（heal over）
examples: The wound healed over.
Time heals over old grief.

words.trans: find the guts to do sth 鼓起勇气；拿出胆量去做某事
examples: She finally found the guts to speak up.
He found the guts to tell the truth.
